A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same wd1 research, with readable main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. v2 substantially extends the work; retained content can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original wd1 training and evaluation results, baseline reproductions, computational measurements, and ablations in Sections 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds wd1++ evaluations, further ablations, and coding experiments in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: v2 introduces wd1++ in Section 3.3. It uses clean completions from intermediate denoising steps, estimates advantages and weights over the expanded completion group, and optimizes a step-conditioned objective. v1's wd1 trains on final completions only.

E1.justification: The four original reasoning benchmarks remain. v2 adds code-generation coverage through AceCode-87K training and HumanEval/MBPP evaluation (Appendix C.3), plus OpenR1-derived training data for the wd1++ MATH500 experiments.

E2.justification: Beyond the original LLaDA, diffu-GRPO, and d1 comparisons, v2 Table 3 adds SDPO on GSM8K and TCR and MDPO on GSM8K/MATH500. MDPO is explicitly reproduced. These materially broaden the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 extends Sudoku training from 5,000 to 12,500 steps and adds that evaluation checkpoint. It introduces full-parameter wd1/wd1++/MDPO experiments alongside the original LoRA setting, with a different system prompt and Math-Verify parsing. New protocols also include verifier rewards for wd1++, its 20-step training result, and coding evaluations with specified generation lengths and diffusion steps.

E4.justification: The original SFT and positive-only ablations are retained in v2 Table 4. New analyses examine policy-ratio estimation versus Monte Carlo sample size, positive/negative weight balance, exponential-weight temperature, and a different-seed MATH training trajectory (Figures 1, 2, 4 and Table 9). These substantially extend the tested design and sensitivity questions.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports a MATH trajectory using a different random seed (Figure 4), without adding aggregate uncertainty estimates for benchmark accuracies. The main seed remains 42. v1's explicit description of reward-plot shading as standard deviation over a 50-step rolling window is no longer provided.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces wd1's 256/512-token Sudoku scores of 25.2/24.2 with 76.4/62.8 after longer training; diffu-GRPO's 512-token Sudoku score changes from 9.3 to 11.7. Table 2 changes wd1 runtime from 82.16 to 81.16 seconds per step. New results include full-tuned wd1++ at 84.5% GSM8K and 44.2% MATH500, additional sensitivity results, and coding scores. Most other original Table 1 scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The original reverse-KL derivation and monotonicity results remain, with renumbering. v2 adds approximation-error bounds, intermediate energy-guidance results, an advantage-weighted concrete-score matching theorem, and an unlearning derivation (Section 4; Appendices A.1, A.3, D.1). The latter contains a sign inconsistency between the log-likelihood penalty in Equation 67 and the DCE expression in Equation 68.

C1.justification: v2's abstract and introduction add wd1++ and the energy-guided diffusion/unlearning interpretation as central contributions. They claim state-of-the-art math performance after 20 training steps and tenfold fewer rollouts. The headline accuracy advantage changes from up to 16% to approximately 59%, although the conclusion retains the older 16% statement.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations involving energy guidance, unlearning, balanced positive/negative weights, and exponential weighting. Appendix D newly discusses identical-reward groups, text-only applicability, and biased likelihood approximation. Conversely, v1's explicit warning that the negative-weight term may alter the monotonic improvement guarantee is no longer retained.

D1.justification: The original wd1/d1 hyperparameters, reward descriptions, and code link are largely retained. v2 adds implementation disclosures for the extensions, including Math-Verify, 8×A800 hardware, wd1++/MDPO batching and rollout accounting in Table 8, and the 200-step AceCode training recipe. These supplement the existing reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 adds a substantive ratio-free optimization discussion covering REINFORCE, RLOO, SPG, and d2, positioning wd1 as an off-policy approach. New energy-guidance and unlearning connections, together with SDPO/TCR/MDPO comparisons, significantly expand its relationship to prior and concurrent research.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the abstract, contribution bullets, likelihood-approximation discussion, and method exposition. It integrates a main-text theory section, moves training-dynamics discussion into Appendix C, reorganizes the appendices, and adds contents, ethics/reproducibility, and limitations sections.

P2.justification: The UCL report is reformatted into the ICLR layout. The opening benchmark bar chart is removed; new policy-ratio and sensitivity plots and a combined results/training-cost display are added. Existing reward and completion-length plots are retained or consolidated in the appendix, and tables are reorganized and expanded beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's d1-focused comparisons: it evaluates wd1++ against additional competitors, tests weighting choices, and demonstrates applicability to coding. These additions materially improve support for the method's usefulness and design. The gains outweigh reporting weaknesses, including inconsistent improvement percentages and the new unlearning derivation's sign inconsistency. Longer training and different fine-tuning settings limit direct performance comparisons between versions.
